title: Want to save some time AND grow your muscles? Supersets are your best friends
summary: NH explains why every program he writes, novice programs included, uses supersets. Pairing non-competing muscles cuts rest time without hurting performance. He covers how to start (bi-sets), how rest works (none inside the superset, 3-4 minutes after), keeping strength work out of supersets, and limits on giant sets.
claims: Supersets are underrated and underused; he puts them in all his programs, even for novices
A superset is simply one exercise followed by another with no rest; adding more exercises eventually becomes a giant set
Supersetting unrelated muscles doesn't lower performance; a set of curls has no effect on calf raises right after. Test it yourself
Most gym time is spent resting, not lifting; supersets reclaim that rest time without cutting warm-ups
Lagging parts like delts can be plugged anywhere as a superset, as long as lateral raises don't follow or precede a press
Pair antagonistic or unrelated muscles; supersetting similar muscle groups is advanced and he rarely does it
Start with bi-sets of two exercises; add more bi-sets through the day and week before moving to tri-sets
Novices can handle 1-2 bi-sets per day of 3 sets each, roughly 12 total sets
Pairing a horizontal press with an elbow extension like skull crushers improves his performance on both
Don't superset strength work or heavy top sets; they need full focus, and they're only a small fraction of total training
There is no rest between exercises within a superset; rest 3-4 minutes after the last exercise before the next round
Doing RDLs then pull-ups as 3 straight sets each with 4-minute rests takes about 24 minutes of rest; as a superset it's about 12
Keep supersets to 4-5 exercises at most; longer ones start eating time instead of saving it
Advanced lifters with good conditioning can skip rest at the end of a long superset because the first exercise has recovered by the time they come back
His own training is all supersets with no rest: he cycles through 5 exercises 4 times, about 7-8 minutes per round
The more lifts in a superset, the more likely they hurt each other's performance; if tonnage stops progressing, the superset is too big
Rather than adding new exercises, combine existing ones in your program into supersets; adding exercises sharply raises tonnage and recovery demand
He can cut about 40 minutes from a 2-hour program with supersets without removing lifts
A giant set is 4 or more exercises; 4-5 is the sweet spot and 6 is overkill
Novices and intermediates should avoid heavy giant sets; giant sets of small muscles (abs, neck, calves, forearms, calisthenics) are fine even for beginners
Don't stack heavy compounds in a giant set, for example rack pulls then pull-ups then DB rows; keep heavy compounds to bi-sets
Starting a giant set with a squat and moving straight to easy exercises builds work capacity and works as high-intensity cardio
If a set of squats leaves you winded, your cardiovascular endurance is low
exercises: superset anywhere except next to a press
easy way to add delt volume
